title: Operator Time: resident history changes the operator available now
summary: OperatorTime is the current synthesis notebook for a motif that first appeared across GAx, state-dependent operator composition, residue/purification, event-owned time and active sensing: fixed substrate parameters can coexist with a changing effective operator because resident history, route, perspective and event state change what is accessible now. Gate 1 isolates the minimum claim with zero parameter drift; Gate 2 shows that frozen symbolic residue acts as serial input whose order induces a later operator trajectory. Gate 3 adds constructive residue synthesis: two individually insufficient provenance-stamped branch residues can jointly expose a useful effective operator outside the branch-only linear span.

nodes.claim: Treats cognition/computation as a trajectory through state-dependent effective operators: theta may stay fixed while resident history changes O_t. The working synthesis links transformer-style context dependence, persistent SELF/reference, transient objects, spectral/frequency accessibility and event-local time without claiming these implementations are equivalent.
nodes.survived: Gate 1 shows the narrow mechanism cleanly: with a fixed synthetic substrate, identical current probe, permanent self anchor and zero parameter drift, recent transient-object class remains linearly accessible from the current operator response at 0.9924 mean accuracy across 64 worlds. Fixed-operator and erased-residue baselines are at chance (0.4956 and 0.4972). Reversing the same two-object history changes the effective operator by 0.0438 relative norm and the current output by 0.2196. Gate 2 then uses matched sequences with the same five token vectors and the same final token: serial reading preserves order at 1.0000 accuracy, while bag-of-symbols, shuffled-order and endpoint-only attackers are at chance (~0.50). Replaying the same sequence into the same reader state is exactly reproducible, while changing prior reader state changes the final operator by 0.0250 relative norm. Gate 3 makes the 'invention' target explicit: branch A alone and branch B alone are exactly chance (0.5000 each), a linear average of their operators is 0.5039, and erasing branch provenance is 0.5000, while nonlinear joint residue synthesis reaches 1.0000. The joint operator sits about 0.0999 relative distance outside the best linear span of the base and branch-only operators, with zero parameter drift and self-anchor fidelity 1.0000.
nodes.killed: A fixed operator cannot recover the recent transient class from the identical present cue, and erasing resident history collapses performance to chance. The repo explicitly does not establish that transformer KV cache is biological short-term memory, that text literally stores operators, that SELF is one vector, that rhythms are operator addresses, or that eigenmodes explain thought. Gate 2 also kills the stronger idea that the stored artifact alone fully specifies the operator: the same sequence can end in a different operator when the reader's prior resident state differs. Gate 3 kills the weaker idea that novelty here is just interpolation: averaging the branch operators remains at chance. It also shows provenance cannot simply be discarded before composition. But the useful bilinear interaction is hand-designed, so the result is a possibility proof, not autonomous invention.

edges.why: The Operator Time README explicitly names GAx/ThirdWay as the earlier route-divergence and context-selected-mode line from which the current operator-time framing grew.
The new repo explicitly identifies state-dependent operator composition as the direct mathematical ancestor of the question 'what determines the operator available at this instant?'
The synthesis reuses the residue/purification line as evidence for the recurring shape resident-state plus computed residue, while keeping the mathematical equivalence claim narrow.
Operator Time explicitly connects active selection of what to sense/probe with the broader idea that current state determines which operation becomes available next.
The new repo imports the persistent-reference/transient-object and event-owned-time framing from SelfAndOtherObjectsInTime into the more general operator-time synthesis.

The README identifies ArtificialCortex/the_whorl as a candidate substrate-level route for replacing software phase/address variables with locally generated field state; this remains a future implementation bridge rather than an established inheritance mechanism.

motifs.title: Resident history determines the operator available now
motifs.description: The fixed substrate can expose different effective operations because recent route, object, perspective and event state remain resident. The motif unifies route divergence, state-dependent operator composition, residue, event-local time and selective sensing without asserting a single biological implementation. Gate 2 adds an externalized version: frozen sequences constrain the trajectory but do not determine it independently of reader state. Gate 3 adds constructive composition: separately insufficient branch residues can jointly activate an operator component outside the branch-only linear span when provenance is preserved.
